metadata.title: The sphere packing problem in dimension 24

nodes.name: Sphere packing density
nodes.statement: The $\emph{density}$ of a sphere packing is the fraction of $\R^n$ covered by congruent balls arranged without overlap of interiors; the sphere packing problem asks for the maximum.

nodes.name: Lattice and periodic packing
nodes.statement: A $\emph{lattice}$ is a discrete subgroup of $\R^n$ of rank $n$; a lattice packing centers spheres at lattice points, and a $\emph{periodic packing}$ is the union of finitely many translates of a lattice.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on $\R^n$
nodes.statement: $\widehat{f}(y) = \int_{\R^n} f(x) e^{-2\pi i \langle x,y \rangle} \, dx$, with $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ the usual inner product on $\R^n$.

nodes.name: Eisenstein series $E_k$
nodes.statement: $E_k(z) = 1 + \frac{2}{\zeta(1-k)}\sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{d \mid n} d^{k-1} e^{2\pi i n z}$; modular form of weight $k$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$ when $k$ is even and $>2$, quasimodular when $k=2$.

nodes.name: Modular discriminant $\Delta$
nodes.statement: $\Delta = (E_4^3 - E_6^2)/1728 = q - 24q^2 + 252 q^3 + O(q^4)$; vanishes nowhere in the upper half plane.

nodes.name: Quasimodular form $\varphi$
nodes.statement: $\varphi = \frac{(25E_4^4 - 49E_6^2 E_4) + 48 E_6 E_4^2 E_2 + (-49 E_4^3 + 25 E_6^2)E_2^2}{\Delta^2}$; weakly holomorphic quasimodular form of weight $-8$ and depth $2$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$.

nodes.name: Slash operator $g|_k M$
nodes.statement: $(g|_k M)(z) = (cz+d)^{-k} g\!\left(\frac{az+b}{cz+d}\right)$ for $g$ on the upper half plane and $M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix} \in \mathrm{SL}_2(\R)$.

nodes.name: Theta functions $\Theta_{00}, \Theta_{01}, \Theta_{10}$
nodes.statement: $\Theta_{00}(z)=\sum_{n\in\Z} e^{\pi i n^2 z}$, $\Theta_{01}(z)=\sum_{n\in\Z}(-1)^n e^{\pi i n^2 z}$, $\Theta_{10}(z)=\sum_{n\in\Z} e^{\pi i (n+1/2)^2 z}$; satisfy Jacobi identity $\Theta_{01}^4+\Theta_{10}^4=\Theta_{00}^4$.

nodes.name: Modular form $\psi_I$ and its $S,T$-images $\psi_S, \psi_T$
nodes.statement: $\psi_I = \frac{7\Theta_{01}^{20}\Theta_{10}^8 + 7\Theta_{01}^{24}\Theta_{10}^4 + 2\Theta_{01}^{28}}{\Delta^2}$; weakly holomorphic modular form of weight $-10$ for $\Gamma(2)$. Set $\psi_S = \psi_I|_{-10}S$ and $\psi_T = \psi_I|_{-10}T$.

nodes.name: Eigenfunction $a(r)$
nodes.statement: $a(r) = -4\sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^{i\infty} \varphi(-1/z) z^{10} e^{\pi i r^2 z}\, dz$ for $r>2$; analytically continued to $\R$ via Lemma~\ref{lemma:plusone}.

nodes.name: Eigenfunction $b(r)$
nodes.statement: $b(r) = -4\sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^{i\infty} \psi_I(z) e^{\pi i r^2 z}\, dz$ for $r>2$; analytically continued to $\R$ via Lemma~\ref{lemma:minusone}.

nodes.name: Optimal auxiliary function $f$
nodes.statement: $f(r) = -\frac{\pi i}{113218560} a(r) - \frac{i}{262080\pi} b(r)$; the linear combination of the $+1$ and $-1$ Fourier eigenfunctions used in Theorem~\ref{thm:LP}.

nodes.name: Auxiliary kernels $A(t)$ and $B(t)$
nodes.statement: $A(t)=\frac{\pi}{28304640}t^{10}\varphi(i/t)-\frac{1}{65520\pi}\psi_I(it)$ and $B(t)=\frac{\pi}{28304640}t^{10}\varphi(i/t)+\frac{1}{65520\pi}\psi_I(it)$, the integral kernels for $f(r)$ and $\widehat{f}(r)$ when $r>2$.

nodes.name: Sphere packing problem in $\R^{24}$
nodes.statement: Find the maximal density of arrangements of congruent balls in $\R^{24}$ with disjoint interiors; equivalently, find the optimal sphere packing in dimension $24$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem (Leech lattice optimality in $\R^{24}$)
nodes.statement: The Leech lattice achieves the optimal sphere packing density in $\R^{24}$, namely $\pi^{12}/12! = 0.0019295743\dots$, and is the unique optimal periodic packing up to scaling and isometries.
conclusions: The Leech lattice achieves the optimal sphere packing density in $\R^{24}$
It is the unique periodic packing in $\R^{24}$ of that density, up to scaling and isometries

nodes.name: Cohn-Elkies linear programming bound
nodes.statement: If $f\colon\R^n\to\R$ is Schwartz with $f(0)=\widehat{f}(0)=1$, $f(x)\le 0$ for $|x|\ge r$, and $\widehat{f}(y)\ge 0$ for all $y$, then the sphere packing density in $\R^n$ is at most $\frac{\pi^{n/2}}{(n/2)!}(r/2)^n$.
conclusions: Sphere packing density in $\R^n$ is at most $\frac{\pi^{n/2}}{(n/2)!}(r/2)^n$

nodes.name: Viazovska's sphere packing theorem in $\R^8$
nodes.statement: The $E_8$ root lattice achieves the optimal sphere packing density in $\R^8$, established by constructing an explicit auxiliary function for the linear programming bound.
conclusions: The $E_8$ lattice is an optimal sphere packing in $\R^8$

nodes.name: Cohn-Elkies uniqueness criterion
nodes.statement: If the auxiliary function $f$ has no roots at distance $2$ or more other than $\sqrt{2k}$ for $k=2,3,\dots$, then the Leech lattice is the unique optimal periodic packing in $\R^{24}$.
conclusions: The Leech lattice is the unique optimal periodic packing in $\R^{24}$

nodes.name: $+1$-eigenfunction lemma
nodes.statement: The function $r\mapsto a(r)$ analytically continues to a holomorphic function on a neighborhood of $\R$; its restriction to $\R$ is a Schwartz function and a radial Fourier eigenfunction in $\R^{24}$ with eigenvalue $1$.
assumptions: $\varphi$ is the quasimodular form of weight $-8$ defined in \eqref{eq:phidef}
conclusions: $a$ extends holomorphically to a neighborhood of $\R$

nodes.name: $-1$-eigenfunction lemma
nodes.statement: The function $r\mapsto b(r)$ analytically continues to a holomorphic function on a neighborhood of $\R$; its restriction to $\R$ is a Schwartz function and a radial Fourier eigenfunction in $\R^{24}$ with eigenvalue $-1$.
assumptions: $\psi_I$ is the modular form of weight $-10$ for $\Gamma(2)$ in \eqref{eq:psiIdef}
$b(r)$ is defined by the integral formula above for $r>2$
conclusions: $b$ extends holomorphically to a neighborhood of $\R$

nodes.name: Negativity of $\varphi(it)$
nodes.section: Appendix A Inequalities for quasimodular forms
nodes.statement: For all $t>0$, $\varphi(it) < 0$.

nodes.name: Inequality $\varphi - (432/\pi^2)\psi_S > 0$
nodes.section: Appendix A Inequalities for quasimodular forms
nodes.statement: For all $t>0$, $\varphi(it) - \frac{432}{\pi^2}\psi_S(it) > 0$.

nodes.name: Leading-term lower bound on $B(t)$
nodes.section: Appendix A Inequalities for quasimodular forms
nodes.statement: For all $t \ge 1$, $B(t) > \frac{1}{39} t e^{2\pi t} - \frac{10}{117\pi} e^{2\pi t}$.

nodes.name: Sinkhorn-style identity for $\varphi$
nodes.statement: Combining quasimodularity \eqref{eq:quasimodular} with periodicity mod $1$, $\varphi(-1/(z+1))(z+1)^{10} - 2\varphi(-1/z)z^{10} + \varphi(-1/(z-1))(z-1)^{10} = 2\varphi(z)$.

nodes.name: Quasimodularity relation for $\varphi$
nodes.statement: $z^8 \varphi(-1/z) = \varphi(z) + \varphi_1(z)/z + \varphi_2(z)/z^2$, with explicit $\varphi_1, \varphi_2$ given in terms of $E_2, E_4, E_6$.

nodes.name: Closed-form for $a(r)$
nodes.statement: $a(r)=4i\sin(\pi r^2/2)^2\big(\widetilde p(r) + \int_0^\infty (\varphi(i/t)t^{10}-p(t))e^{-\pi r^2 t}\,dt\big)$, with $\widetilde p$ the explicit rational function in $r$.

nodes.name: Integral form of $f(r)$ for $r>2$
nodes.statement: $f(r) = \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^\infty A(t) e^{-\pi r^2 t}\, dt$ for $r>2$.

nodes.name: Integral form of $\widehat f(r)$ for $r>\sqrt 2$
nodes.statement: $\widehat f(r) = \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^\infty B(t) e^{-\pi r^2 t}\, dt$ for $r>\sqrt 2$, by analytic continuation.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:plusone} ($+1$-eigenfunction)
nodes.statement: Substitute $-4\sin^2(\pi r^2/2) = e^{\pi i r^2}-2+e^{-\pi i r^2}$, shift contours, apply quasimodularity \eqref{eq:quasimodular}, then change variables $w=-1/z$ to obtain $\widehat a = a$ and Schwartz decay.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:minusone} ($-1$-eigenfunction)
nodes.statement: Following Proposition~6 of \cite{V}, substitute the trigonometric expansion, shift contours using $\psi_I(z\pm1)=\psi_T(z)$ and $\psi_T-\psi_I=-\psi_S$, then apply $\psi_I|_{-10}S=\psi_S$ etc.\ to deduce $\widehat b=-b$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} (Leech optimality)
nodes.statement: Construct $f = -\frac{\pi i}{113218560} a - \frac{i}{262080\pi} b$; verify the Cohn-Elkies hypotheses for $r=2$ via inequalities on $A(t)$ and $B(t)$; combine with the uniqueness criterion of \cite{CE}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:phinonpos} ($\varphi(it)<0$)
nodes.statement: Split into $t \ge 1$ and $t \le 1$; multiply by $\Delta^2$, truncate the $q$-series at $n=50$ with explicit coefficient bounds, replace factors of $\pi$ and $t$ by rational bounds, then apply Sturm's theorem.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:ineq2} ($\varphi-432\psi_S/\pi^2>0$)
nodes.statement: Same Sturm-theorem-on-truncated-$q$-series technique as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:phinonpos}, applied to $(\varphi-432\psi_S/\pi^2)\Delta^2$; for $t\le 1$ reduce via \eqref{eq:quasimodular} and \eqref{eq:psiSdef}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Bleadingterms}
nodes.statement: Multiply $B(t)-\big(\frac{1}{39}te^{2\pi t}-\frac{10}{117\pi}e^{2\pi t}\big)$ by $\Delta^2$; the standard truncation bound gives error $\le 10^{-50}q^6$, and Sturm's theorem confirms positivity.

nodes.name: Ansatz for $\varphi$
nodes.statement: $\Delta^2 \varphi$ is sought as a holomorphic quasimodular form of weight $16$ and depth $2$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$; this five-dimensional space (spanned by $E_4^4, E_6^2 E_4, E_6 E_4^2 E_2, E_4^3 E_2^2, E_6^2 E_2^2$) and the asymptotic constraints \eqref{eq:phiovertinfty}, \eqref{eq:phiovertzero} pin down $\varphi$ up to a constant.

nodes.name: Ansatz for $\psi_I$
nodes.statement: $\Delta^2 \psi_I$ is sought as a holomorphic modular form of weight $14$ for $\Gamma(2)$; the eight-dimensional space and the linear constraint $\psi_S+\psi_T=\psi_I$ together with asymptotics determine $\psi_I$ up to a constant.

nodes.name: Cohn-Miller numerical conjectures
nodes.statement: The quadratic Taylor coefficients $-14347/5460$ for $f$ and $-205/156$ for $\widehat f$, the value $1/156$ at $\sqrt 2$ and the derivative formulas at $\sqrt 2$ and $2$ match the conjectured special values from \cite{CM}, including $f'(2) = -1/16380$ from Lemma~5.1 of \cite{CM}.

nodes.name: Coefficient bounds for $E_2, E_4, E_6, \Theta^4$
nodes.statement: The coefficient of $q^n$ is bounded by $24(n+1)^2$ in $E_2$, by $240(n+1)^4$ in $E_4$, by $504(n+1)^6$ in $E_6$, and the coefficient of $q^{n/2}$ in $\Theta_{00}^4$, $\Theta_{01}^4$, $\Theta_{10}^4$ is at most $24(n+1)^2$.

nodes.name: Sturm-theorem-on-truncated-$q$-series verification
nodes.statement: Procedure for verifying inequalities for quasimodular forms on the imaginary axis by truncating the $q$-series, controlling the truncation error, replacing $\pi$ and $t$ by rational bounds, and applying Sturm's theorem in PARI/GP.
input: A quasimodular/modular form expression $F(it)$ to be sign-tested
A truncation level $n_0$ (we use $n_0 = 50$) and the corresponding $q$-series for $F\Delta^2$
output: A rigorous proof that the inequality holds on the imaginary axis
nodes.pseudocode:
1. Multiply $F$ by $\Delta^2$ to clear denominators.
2. Compute the $q$-series of $F\Delta^2$ up to $q^{n_0-1}$ with exact rational arithmetic.
3. Bound the tail $\sum_{n\ge n_0} |\text{coef}_n| q^n$ using the polynomial coefficient bounds for $E_2, E_4, E_6, \Theta^4$.
4. Replace any factor of $\pi$ by a rational lower/upper bound (e.g.\ $\lfloor 10^{10}\pi\rfloor/10^{10}$) chosen by sign.
5. Replace $t$ by rational bounds (e.g.\ $1\le t\le 1/(23 q^{1/2})$) for the regime $t\le 1$ via $z\mapsto -1/z$.
6. Apply Sturm's theorem to the resulting rational polynomial (in $q$ or $q^{1/2}$) to verify the absence of sign changes on the appropriate interval.

nodes.name: Trigonometric identity substitution
nodes.statement: Substitute $-4\sin^2(\pi r^2/2)=e^{\pi i r^2}-2+e^{-\pi i r^2}$ into the defining integral for $a(r)$, splitting it into three contour integrals.

nodes.name: Contour shift
nodes.statement: Shift contours in the three integrals from $[-1, i\infty-1]$, $[0,i\infty]$, $[1,i\infty+1]$ to integrals over $[\cdot,i]$ and $[i,i\infty]$ as in Proposition~2 of \cite{V}.

nodes.name: Apply quasimodularity identity
nodes.statement: Use \eqref{eq:quasimodular} and periodicity mod $1$ to derive the identity $\varphi(-1/(z+1))(z+1)^{10}-2\varphi(-1/z)z^{10}+\varphi(-1/(z-1))(z-1)^{10}=2\varphi(z)$ (Lemma~\ref{LP401.6}-style).

nodes.name: Analytic continuation and Schwartz decay
nodes.statement: Combine the identity with the asymptotic bounds \eqref{eq:phiovertinfty} and \eqref{eq:phiovertzero} to obtain \eqref{eq:conta}, the holomorphic extension to a neighborhood of $\R$, and exponential decay of $a$ and all derivatives.

nodes.name: Compute $24$-D radial Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Replace $e^{\pi i r^2 z}$ by $z^{-12} e^{\pi i r^2(-1/z)}$ inside each integral of \eqref{eq:conta} to write $\widehat a(r)$ as a sum of contour integrals.

nodes.name: Change of variable $w=-1/z$
nodes.statement: Apply $w=-1/z$ to recognise each integral as one of the four integrals in \eqref{eq:conta} (with shifts using periodicity mod $1$); conclude $\widehat a = a$.

nodes.name: Substitute trig identity and shift contours
nodes.statement: Replace $-4\sin^2(\pi r^2/2)$ by $e^{-\pi i r^2}-2+e^{\pi i r^2}$ and shift contours in the defining integral of $b(r)$, using $\psi_I(z\pm 1)=\psi_T(z)$, to express $b(r)$ in terms of $\psi_T$ and $\psi_I$ on $[\cdot,i]\cup[i,i\infty]$.

nodes.name: Apply $\psi_T-\psi_I=-\psi_S$
nodes.statement: Use the linear relation $\psi_S+\psi_T=\psi_I$ (Jacobi identity) to rewrite the tail integral over $[i,i\infty]$ in terms of $\psi_S$, yielding the analytic continuation and Schwartz decay of $b$.

nodes.name: Compute $24$-D Fourier transform and change variables
nodes.statement: Replace $e^{\pi i r^2 z}$ by $z^{-12} e^{\pi i r^2(-1/z)}$, then change variables $w=-1/z$, transforming each integrand by the slash action of $S$.

nodes.name: Use $\psi_I|_{-10}S=\psi_S$ etc. to conclude $\widehat b = -b$
nodes.statement: Apply $\psi_I|_{-10}S=\psi_S$, $\psi_S|_{-10}S=\psi_I$, and $\psi_T|_{-10}S=-\psi_T$ to identify the transformed integrals with $-b(r)$.

nodes.name: Define $f$ and verify normalization / root structure
nodes.statement: Set $f = -\frac{\pi i}{113218560} a - \frac{i}{262080\pi} b$; verify $f(0)=\widehat f(0)=1$, the Taylor coefficients $-14347/5460, -205/156$, and that $f, \widehat f$ have double roots at $\sqrt{2k}$ for $k\ge 2$ except a simple root of $f$ at $r=2$.

nodes.name: Reduce $f(r)\le 0$ to $A(t)\le 0$
nodes.statement: Use \eqref{eq:a2} and \eqref{eq:b2} to write $f(r) = \sin^2(\pi r^2/2)\int_0^\infty A(t) e^{-\pi r^2 t}\,dt$ for $r>2$; reduce $f\le 0$ on $[2,\infty)$ to $A(t)\le 0$ for $t\ge 0$.

nodes.name: Reduce $A\le 0$ to $\varphi(it)\le 0$
nodes.statement: Rewrite $A(t)$ as $\frac{\pi t^{10}}{28304640}(\varphi(i/t) + \frac{432}{\pi^2}\psi_S(i/t))$; since $\psi_S(it)\le 0$ from its formula, reduce to $\varphi(it)\le 0$, which is Lemma~\ref{lemma:phinonpos}.

nodes.name: Show $\widehat f \ge 0$ on $[\sqrt 2,\infty)$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:fhatB} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:ineq2} ($B(t)\ge 0$), $\widehat f(r)\ge 0$ for $r\ge \sqrt 2$; the integral converges for $r>\sqrt 2$ because the $e^{4\pi t}$ terms cancel in $B$.

nodes.name: Handle $\widehat f(r)\ge 0$ on $(0,\sqrt 2)$
nodes.statement: Subtract $\frac{1}{39} t e^{2\pi t} - \frac{10}{117\pi} e^{2\pi t}$ from $B$ over $[1,\infty)$; the subtracted contribution evaluates to a nonnegative explicit function on $(0,\sqrt 2)$, and the remaining integrals are nonnegative by Lemma~\ref{lemma:Bleadingterms} and $B(t)\ge 0$ on $[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Apply Cohn-Elkies bound and uniqueness
nodes.statement: Conclude via Theorem~\ref{thm:LP} that the Leech lattice density is optimal, and via the Section~8 argument of \cite{CE} that, since the only roots $r\ge 2$ of $f$ are at $\sqrt{2k}$ ($k\ge 2$), the Leech lattice is the unique optimal periodic packing.

nodes.name: Sturm theorem on truncated polynomial ($t\ge 1$)
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma$ be the partial sum for $n<50$; verify with Sturm's theorem that $\sigma + 10^{-50} q^6$ has no sign change on $(0,1/535)$ and is negative as $q\to 0$, proving $\varphi(it)<0$ for $t\ge 1$.

nodes.name: Case $t\le 1$: reduce via $z\mapsto -1/z$
nodes.statement: Use \eqref{eq:10overt} to convert $\varphi(it)<0$ for $t\le 1$ to $-t^2 \varphi(it) + i t \varphi_1(it) + \varphi_2(it) > 0$ for $t\ge 1$.

nodes.name: Sturm theorem on truncated polynomial in $q^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: Replace $\pi$ by $\lfloor 10^{10}\pi\rfloor/10^{10}$ or $\lceil 10^{10}\pi\rceil/10^{10}$ by sign and bound $1\le t\le 1/(23 q^{1/2})$; truncate at $n=50$ with error $\le 10^{-50} q^6$ and apply Sturm's theorem on $(0,1/23)$.

nodes.name: Clear denominators by multiplying by $\Delta^2$
nodes.statement: Multiply the form $F$ by $\Delta^2$ so that the resulting $q$-series has polynomially-bounded integer (or rational) coefficients.

nodes.name: Truncate $q$-series and bound tail
nodes.statement: Compute the partial sum of $F\Delta^2$ for $n<n_0$ (we use $n_0=50$) and bound the omitted terms using the polynomial coefficient bounds for $E_2, E_4, E_6$ and $\Theta_{ij}^4$; here the bound is $\le 10^{-50} q^6$.

nodes.name: Replace $\pi$ and $t$ by rational bounds
nodes.statement: Replace $\pi$ by $\lfloor 10^{10}\pi\rfloor/10^{10}$ or $\lceil 10^{10}\pi\rceil/10^{10}$ depending on sign; bound $t$ by $1\le t\le 1/(23 q^{1/2})$ in the regime $t\le 1$ to obtain a rational polynomial in $q$ or $q^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Apply Sturm's theorem in PARI/GP
nodes.statement: Use Sturm's theorem with exact rational arithmetic in PARI/GP (ancillary file \texttt{appendix.txt}) to verify the truncated polynomial has no sign change on the relevant interval, completing the rigorous inequality proof.
